headline: Highest risk is data leakage and capability conflict: Goose can share filesystem state and broad egress with slim, which also writes sensitive container artifacts.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP, while slim reads/writes container artifacts and files. A shared filesystem bridge makes prompt injection plausible if slim outputs are later treated as instructions by Goose. No direct evidence of a parser bridge exists, so this is inferred from documented surfaces on both agents.
conditions: IF Goose ingests slim-generated files from the shared workspace as instructions
IF slim writes attacker-controlled text into files Goose later parses
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Require manual review of slim outputs before Goose reads them
Prefix all machine-generated files with a non-executable format marker
Disable MCP paths that read shared workspace files
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to inter-agent files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd with broad network egress; slim touches container images, filesystem artifacts, certificate private keys, and registry credentials. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive build artifacts can leak through Goose’s outbound model/provider or MCP paths. The pairwise leakage pathway is credible from both profiles, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF Goose is pointed at the same directory that contains slim’s certificate private keys or registry credentials
IF Goose sends workspace contents to configured model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Move secrets out of the shared workspace
Rotate any registry credentials used during slim runs
Run Goose with a scrubbed directory containing no private keys
Restrict Goose network egress during slim processing
requires-engineering: enforce secret redaction before any outbound call

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, and modify_git_state; slim also has shell, read/write filesystem, and broad network egress. Goose’s shared_state_with_other_instances is via filesystem, while slim has no shared-state protection. Concurrent writes to the same repo or artifacts can corrupt git state or build outputs, and the profiles do not show locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout
IF Goose and slim write to the same artifact directory without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Pause one agent while the other mutates git state
Use a lock file around shared writes
Commit from only one agent per branch
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code or operational instructions, and slim can execute shell commands and manipulate container artifacts. If slim treats Goose’s output as authoritative, an error in Goose can cascade into incorrect image slimming or destructive commands. The profiles do not show verification between them, but the action-taking pathway is present.
conditions: IF slim executes commands derived from Goose output without human verification
IF Goose’s generated file edits are fed directly into slim’s container-processing workflow
mitigations: Require a human approval step before slim executes Goose-derived commands
Compare Goose output against the original source before acting
Limit slim to dry-run mode for first pass
Keep Goose outputs in a review-only folder
requires-engineering: add schema validation for Goose-produced instructions

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles model provider keys and extension tokens, while slim handles registry credentials and certificate private keys. If both are run on the same regulated workspace, retention and residency obligations can diverge across secrets and build artifacts. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR status, so this is a documented-policy mismatch risk rather than a confirmed violation.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or private keys are present in the shared workspace
IF Goose or slim logs or retains those secrets beyond the operator’s policy
mitigations: Store regulated secrets outside the shared workspace
Review retention settings for both tools before use
Delete temporary artifacts after each run
Use separate credentials for each agent
requires-engineering: align logging and retention policies
